title: Common millet domestication at Cishan
summary: Storage pits at Cishan, in Hebei, China, held common millet remains that a 2009 study dated to as early as about 10,000 years ago, with its oldest dates at 10,400 to 10,100 calibrated years before present, pushing back evidence of millet farming in East Asia. The dating is disputed: another paper places early domestication by about 8700 cal BP and the Cishan pits at about 8000 to 7500 years ago.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree: oldest occupation 10,400-10,100 cal BP and community span to 7500 cal BP in one source; the pits at 8000-7500 cal BP in another. cal BP counts from 1950 CE.

where.modern_name: Cishan site, near Wu'an, Hebei, China
where.historical_name: Cishan Neolithic village, North China Plain

importance.justification: One of the earliest sites with stored millet in China, central to debates on the origin of agriculture in North China.
